{{Top|ca|leg}}
{{Quote|It is extremely difficult to employ in combat and is derived from the teachings of Zelashiel the Blasphemer in the Holocron of Darth Revan.|Darth Bane, on the Force power drain life|<ref name="BoS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>
}}
'''Zelashiel''', also referred to as '''Zelashiel the Blasphemer''', was a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] individual who wielded the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of]] [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. One of the [[Force power/Legends|Force techniques]] that Zelashiel was proficient in was the ability to [[Force drain/Legends|drain an individual's essence]], a delicate procedure that was exceedingly difficult to use in combat. Zelashiel's teachings eventually were detailed in the [[Darth Revan's Sith Holocron|Sith Holocron]] of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] around the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Jedi Civil War]].<ref name="BoS" />

Sometime between [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] and [[980 BBY]],<ref name="Date">The [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan|Seventh Battle]] of [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]] happened in [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. Darth Bane studied Revan's holocron shortly before the battle, and the novel ''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]'' places Bane's death in [[980 BBY]]. Thus, Bane must have composed ''The Rule of Two'', the essay in which Zelashiel is mentioned, sometime in those two decades.</ref> Zelashiel's instructions were commented on in an [[The Rule of Two|essay]] authored by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]],<ref name="BoS" /> who had studied Revan's [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] before destroying it.<ref name="DB:PoD">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref> Many [[Standard year/Legends|years]] later, Bane's essay, including his notes on Zelashiel, was added to the ''[[Book of Sith]]'', a compilation of historical writings collected in one volume by [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]].<ref name="BoS" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Drain life: This ability saps the life energy from a target. It is supposedly derived from the teachings of "Zelashiel the Blasphemer," a new character whose name is meant to sound slightly Hebrew; specifically a name that might fit amid this list of theological angels) to evoke the sense that he was a Chosen One who fell from grace. Totally overthinking a forgettable one-sentence reference, I realize.|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="Endnotes 3">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2012/03/endnotes-for-star-wars-book-of-sith_30.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: Book of Sith (part 3)}}</ref>}}
Zelashiel was first mentioned in the resource guide ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'', which was written by [[Daniel Wallace]]. In his third series of endnotes about the book, Wallace mentioned that the character's name was created to sound similar to a [[Wikipedia:Theophoric names|theophoric]] [[Wikipedia:Hebrew language|Hebrew]] name. Wallace also noted that Zelashiel was named such so that the reader could get a sense that the character had experienced a fall from grace. The author further speculated that the character of Zelashiel either preceded the Sith [[King/Legends|King]] [[Adas]] or was simply a mythical legend.<ref name="Endnotes 3" />
